statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band after a record Nasdaq-100 close that faded off its session high.
recommendation: Tail at 11% maps to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The published forecast carries a WATCH band across the 17:00-20:00 UTC sequence on 7 October covering the 10-year note auction and the September FOMC minutes, where Tail is modelled conditionally at 20-23%.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes at a record but fades off its high; Tail stays low into the September FOMC minutes
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed 6 October at a record 31,224.69, up 148.24 points or 0.48%, with the S&P 500 at 7,818.93 (+0.58%) and the Nasdaq Composite at 27,599.89 (+0.45%) also setting records. The session gapped above the prior 31,076.44 close and held that gap, but it peaked at 31,361.37 and faded roughly 137 points to finish near the 31,208.20 session low. That observed retracement, together with VIX at 15.01 (-3.29%), is the opposite of the no-retracement structure that Tail measures, so Tail is assessed at 11%. Stress is held at 45% because the environment remains genuinely difficult beneath the record prints: the 30-year yield sits near 5.64-5.66%, its highest since 2002, the 10-year eased to 5.27% only after touching a 2002 high above 5.30%, Brent remains above 100 dollars with the Strait of Hormuz still largely blocked, and the September FOMC delivered a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% into subsequently softening labour data. Leadership was concentrated in semiconductors and AI-linked power, with Nvidia and AMD at all-time highs, Marvell higher on a raised fiscal-2028 revenue target and Constellation Energy up more than 12% on a 20-year, 4.3 billion dollar Google nuclear agreement. The dominant mode is recorded as mixed: the daily trend is up, yet the close faded to the lower end of the session range. The principal checkpoint inside the forecast window is the release of the September FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on 7 October, preceded by a 10-year note auction at 17:00 UTC. Because October hike odds have fallen from roughly 70% to about 20% since that meeting, a hawkish minutes read is a credible repricing mechanism, and the forecast therefore carries a conditional WATCH band from 17:00 to 20:00 UTC rather than a block.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail rose from 8-12% through the Asian and European hours of 6 October to a 22% peak at 15:00 UTC as the U.S. session extended, with the 15:00 and 16:00 UTC slots mapping to WATCH, then decayed to 11% by 22:00 UTC as the index faded off its high into the close. Stress held in a narrow 45-48% band throughout and Confidence stayed at 86-88%, while dominant mode shifted from mixed to trend-up during the U.S. session and back to mixed after the fade.
outlookSummary: Overnight and European hours are modelled with Tail at 10-14% on contained two-way ranges. Tail lifts to 15-18% across the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open and the first cash hours for opening-range expansion, then to a conditional 20-23% WATCH band from the 17:00 UTC 10-year note auction through the 18:00 UTC September FOMC minutes and the following power hour. Risk decays to 13-17% after the 20:00 UTC cash close. Stress tracks Tail higher to a 52% peak around the minutes, and Confidence eases from 87% to 86% as live price-path evidence ages. No post-event price structure is treated as observed.

forecast.analysis: Post-close Globex hour. The Nasdaq-100 settled at a record 31,224.69 (+0.48%) but finished near its 31,208.20 session low after fading about 137 points off the 31,361.37 high, so mean reversion is working rather than failing. VIX 15.01 and flat oil keep Tail low.

VIX 15.01 (-3.29%), no volatility expansion observed
